record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Analogue of F-QSO theorem for ξ-QSOs
record.original_question: Let ξ = {E_1, ..., E_q} be a partition of the species set E, and define a ξ-QSO by requiring P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever both parent indices i and j lie in the same block E_p. Determine whether an analogue of Theorem 5 holds for every ξ-QSO; that is, whether such operators always have a unique fixed point and whether every trajectory converges to it, as happens for F-QSOs.

evidence.quote: Theorem 5. [39] Any F -QSO has a unique fixed point (1, 0, ..., 0) (with m zeros). Besides, for any x0 ∈ S m , the trajectory {x(n) } tends to this fixed point exponentially rapidly.

Problem 10. Consider a partition ξ = {E1 , ..., Eq } of E i.e., E = E1 ∪...∪Eq , Ei ∩Ej = ∅, i 6= j. Assume Pij,k = 0 if i, j ∈ Ep , for p = 1, ..., q. Call the corresponding operator a ξ−QSO. Is an analogue of Theorem 5 true for any ξ−QSO?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m\ge 2$ and let $E=\{1,2,\dots,m\}$ be a finite set (the species set). Denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex by
$$S^{m-1}=\Bigl\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m:\ x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\Bigr\}.$$
A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$(Vx)_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^{m} P_{ij,k}\,x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the heredity coefficients satisfy
$$P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{m}P_{ij,k}=1\quad\text{for all }i,j.$$
For $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$, the trajectory is the sequence $x^{(n+1)}=Vx^{(n)}$, $n\ge 0$.

Now fix a partition $\xi=\{E_1,\dots,E_q\}$ of $E$, i.e.\ $E=E_1\cup\cdots\cup E_q$ with $E_p\cap E_r=\emptyset$ for $p\ne r$. A QSO is called a $\xi$-QSO if its coefficients additionally satisfy
$$P_{ij,k}=0\quad\text{whenever there exists } p\in\{1,\dots,q\}\text{ such that } i,j\in E_p.$$

Question: Is it true that, for every partition $\xi$ of $E$ and every $\xi$-QSO $V$, the operator $V$ has a unique fixed point in $S^{m-1}$ and every trajectory $\{x^{(n)}\}_{n\ge 0}$ starting from any $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$ converges to that fixed point?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works have studied ξ-QSOs (and the related ξ(s)- and ξ(a)-QSOs) on the 2-dimensional simplex, classifying them into multiple nonconjugate classes and analyzing dynamics for several specific partitions/classes. These studies reveal varied dynamical behaviors (including non-unique fixed points and non-global convergence in some classes), so the proposed analogue of the F-QSO theorem does not hold uniformly. A complete general answer for arbitrary partitions ξ and arbitrary dimension does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: On ξ(s)-Quadratic Stochastic Operators on Two-Dimensional Simplex and Their Behavior
status_evidence.snippet: ξ(s)-QSO is defined on 2D simplex; classified into 20 nonconjugate classes; dynamics of three classes investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classification and dynamics for ξ-type QSOs on 2D simplex are known.

status_evidence.title: Global and local behavior of a class of ξ(s)-QSO
status_evidence.snippet: Describes and classifies operators generated by additional partitions on 2D simplex.
status_evidence.claim: Researchers continue to handle particular partitions case-by-case rather than via a single uniform theorem.

status_evidence.title: Genetic Algebras Associated with ξ(a)-Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies ξ(a)-QSOs and their associated structures.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to investigate variants of ξ-QSOs without claiming a general analogue of the F-QSO unique fixed-point theorem.
